query: How can we reduce incident resolution time?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Grouping incidents by type is a strong axis for finding which categories drive long resolution times. Values are well-grounded in short_description (VPN, database, email, WiFi->network_access all correct).

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: Technician performance is relevant to resolution time, but this appears largely redundant with the existing assigned_to/closed_by columns. Values like 'Beth Anglin' cannot be derived from the shown source text (only timestamps and description), suggesting they are copied from another column or invented; not warranted by the evidence samples.

per_column.name: resolution_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (single_user vs department_wide) is a useful axis correlated with effort. Department-wide is reasonably inferred where text names a department, but 'single_user' for 'VPN connection issue' and 'infrastructure_wide' being the dominant value are often not supported by silent text, indicating over-confident inference.

per_column.name: incident_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity is highly relevant to resolution time. However the values are speculative: labeling 'Cannot connect to database' as 'access_denial' vs an email issue as 'service_outage' reflects heuristic guessing rather than stated severity; the original priority column already carries grounded severity information.

per_column.name: technician_reassignment
per_column.rationale: Reassignment is a plausible driver of delay, but the source text provides no basis for a true/false reassignment flag; every sample is 'True' with no supporting evidence, indicating fabrication.

per_column.name: incident_closure_status
per_column.rationale: Derivable from state/closed_at, so grounded, but it is trivially redundant with the existing 'state' and 'closed_at' columns and adds little new analytical leverage.

per_column.name: caller_context
per_column.rationale: Named vs system user is a mild segmentation axis but largely restates caller_id/sys_updated_by info; groundedness is moderate as classification from IDs is plausible but not shown in the evidence text.

per_column.name: infrastructure_layer_affected
per_column.rationale: Layer (network/application/database) is a reasonable analytical grouping and is well-mapped from short_description, though it partly overlaps with incident_category.

judge.rationale: The set offers several genuinely useful grouping axes for resolution-time analysis (incident_category, infrastructure_layer, severity, scope). However groundedness is mixed: category and layer are soundly extracted from short_description, but assigned_technician, technician_reassignment, and severity/scope frequently assert specifics the shown source text does not support, indicating fabricated or over-confident inferred values. A few columns (closure_status, caller_context) are grounded but largely redundant with existing original columns.
